name: AceBrix
headline: Five pathways, one shared library. We map yours with you rather than guessing it.
situation: Every Toggle Bespoke engagement runs off one library of 21 lessons and five pathways through it. Which one fits depends on where you are starting and what you need working by Monday, so we would rather scope it with you than assume it. The five modules below sit in three or more of the five pathways, so wherever you begin, you will do these.

pathway.name: We will map it with you
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive, scoped in a short conversation first
pathway.why: We do not guess the pathway from a form. A short conversation about your team, your tools and what you need working by Monday decides it, and the depth is set separately on its own dial.

pillars.title: Five ways in
pillars.body: P1 starts with AI literacy and P2 with Marketing Fundamentals. P3 applies AI across a marketing function, P4 is the founder's route through everything at pace, and P5 puts AI inside your operations. Five different starting points, and none of them is a level.

pillars.title: One shared backbone
pillars.body: The five modules below appear in three or more of the five pathways, so the core of the weekend is the same wherever you begin. What changes is what gets built around it.

pillars.title: The depth dial
pillars.body: Every lesson runs on an ELI 15 to 30 setting, so the same module can be a plain introduction or a deep technical build. We set it to the people in the room.

pillars.title: A weekend, not a retainer
pillars.body: The engagement is one intensive weekend where senior marketers build the thing with your team, document it, and support you for 30 days after. You own the accounts, the data and the system afterwards.

modules.name: AI Basics
modules.why: The shared starting point in four of the five pathways, so everyone works from the same picture.

modules.name: Prompting and Tools
modules.why: The practical skill that makes every later module faster, whichever pathway you take.

modules.name: Agentic AI and Claude Code
modules.why: The one module in all five pathways, because handing whole tasks to an agent changes any job.

modules.name: AI CRM and Conversations
modules.why: Every organisation has enquiries and follow-ups, and this is where the quickest wins usually sit.

modules.name: Build Your Workflow
modules.why: The closing module in three pathways, where the weekend becomes a written workflow you keep using.

outcomes: Name which of the five pathways fits you, and say why
List the three tasks in your week AI should take over first
Explain to your team what a one-weekend intensive would actually change
Come to a short scoping call with a specific goal instead of general interest

proof.label: EduKids, e-commerce and education
proof.body: EduKids was stuck under a 4x return on TikTok and hit its 6x target by month two, alongside RM14,000 in monthly website revenue and a steady 5.5% conversion rate. It is relevant to anyone here because the gain came from method, testing and tightening rather than from a bigger budget.

name: Ayu Borneo
sector: Local services, massage and head-spa outlets
headline: Fill appointment slots outlet by outlet, and build a Klang Valley name from a Sabah base.
situation: You run massage and head-spa outlets across Kota Kinabalu and the Klang Valley, with an established presence on TikTok and Xiaohongshu and creator coverage behind it. The commercial job is different from awareness: every empty slot in a day is revenue that does not come back. In a new market you are also building recognition outlet by outlet, catchment by catchment.

pathway.name: Owner's Fast-Track
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive with the owner on Owner's Fast-Track (P4), with AI for Marketers (P3) as a follow-on for the marketing lead
pathway.why: The owner needs practical decisions about where spend and attention go across outlets, which is what Fast-Track gives. The person publishing daily goes deeper on the applied track afterwards, and both meet on the same documented routine.

pillars.title: Two tracks, one routine
pillars.body: The owner learns to set direction, judge output and read numbers. The marketing lead takes the full production and ads craft on the applied track afterwards, finishing on the same documented routine, so briefs and reviews take minutes.

pillars.title: Slots, not just followers
pillars.body: Attention is already there, so we point it at bookings for specific days and times. Quiet weekday hours get their own offers and their own creative.

pillars.title: Outlet by outlet targeting
pillars.body: Every outlet sits in its own catchment with its own demand, and a chain your size cannot run them off one national campaign. You leave able to launch and read each location on its own without rebuilding anything.

pillars.title: A new market from a known base
pillars.body: Klang Valley customers do not know you yet, so the content has to establish the experience before it asks for a booking. We build a launch sequence you can reuse for the next outlet you open.

modules.why: The owner and the marketing lead leave with the same vocabulary, so a brief across five outlets needs no translating.

modules.why: Judge AI output quickly, and know what still needs a human eye.

modules.why: A tool stack that suits a multi-outlet chain, not an enterprise.

See which outlet is winning bookings and which needs help
Reply to booking enquiries fast without hiring for it
Reuse one launch sequence the next time you open a location

proof.body: Kith and Kin's campaigns worked because they were drawn tight around a single Kuala Lumpur catchment instead of the whole city, which is what kept the cost per enquiry down. Radius, not reach, is the call you make once per outlet, across the whole estate.

name: Damia Nash
sector: Beauty content creator, TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and Lemon8
headline: A commercial layer under the audience you already built, so attention becomes income you can plan.
situation: The audience is built, across four platforms, and kept. This is about the business underneath it: a clear offer, pricing you can defend, a way to capture demand you own, and the few numbers that tell you what is working. The content half is already yours.

pathway.name: Marketing Fundamentals
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive built around your own brand and rate card
pathway.why: Marketing Fundamentals is the track that puts structure under a brand, which is the half that turns reach into revenue you can forecast. Everything is built against your actual platforms and your actual rate card, not a case study.

pillars.title: Price your brand deals
pillars.body: You learn to put a defensible number on reach, engagement, exclusivity and usage rights, so quotes stop coming from a feeling. A rate card is much easier to hold when you can show how you built it.

pillars.title: An offer that is yours
pillars.body: Brand deals depend on somebody else's budget cycle. We work on something you own, a product, a service or a paid community, so there is income nobody has to approve.

pillars.title: From audience to contacts
pillars.body: Your followers live on platforms you do not control and cannot export. You leave with a simple path from a post to a contact list you can reach directly.

pillars.title: Numbers past views
pillars.body: Views are where the question starts, not where it ends. You learn the handful of numbers that show whether attention is converting, and a ten minute weekly check to keep an eye on them.

modules.why: Get your audience, offer and positioning written down, so it reads as a brand rather than a feed.

modules.name: Performance Basics
modules.why: Learn how paid works from the inside, both for your own offers and for reading what brands ask of you.

modules.why: Already your strongest ground, so we go light and use it to tighten planning across four platforms.

outcomes: Send a rate card with the reasoning behind every number
Describe one offer you own, priced, in a single paragraph
Capture contacts from a post instead of losing them in comments
Run a ten minute weekly check on the numbers that matter

proof.label: Al Hidayah, content plus somewhere to buy
proof.body: Al Hidayah put a shop and paid support behind content that was already working, and orders rose 200% in four months. Content was never their problem either. The gain came from having somewhere for attention to land.

name: Destinasi TV
sector: Travel and food media, over one million followers
headline: You already make shows people watch. Two modules to make more of them, faster, and reach further.
situation: You have solved the part nobody can shortcut. Mat Salleh Cari Makan and the shows around it earn attention on their own, which is the thing most brands try to buy and fail at. The opening sits on either side of that strength: producing at higher volume without adding crew, and putting spend behind the episodes that have already proven themselves.

pathway.name: Selected modules
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive scoped to two modules, with your production and social team
pathway.why: A focused engagement rather than a full pathway, because throughput and the paid layer are the two places we can add to what you already do. Everything else in the library would be teaching you your own job.

pillars.title: The craft stays yours
pillars.body: Nothing here changes how you make a show or who decides what is funny. AI sits around the edit, on the repetitive parts, so taste and judgement stay with your team.

pillars.title: More cuts per shoot
pillars.body: One trip should fill more than one slot. You learn to generate vertical cuts, thumbnails, subtitles and alternate hooks quickly, so a single production day covers a longer schedule.

pillars.title: Paid behind what already works
pillars.body: Organic tells you which episode landed, which is better information than any targeting guess. Paid takes that same clip to people who have never seen the show, in Malaysia and beyond.

pillars.title: Amplification you can plan
pillars.body: Reach you chose is worth more than reach that happened, because you can repeat it. Being able to plan amplification and show what it returned turns a good month into a method.

modules.name: AI Creative and Visuals
modules.why: Get more finished assets out of every shoot, from vertical cuts and thumbnails to alternate hooks for the same episode.

modules.name: AI Ads and Performance
modules.why: Put budget behind the episodes that already performed, and read the result well enough to do it again next month.

outcomes: Ship several formats of one episode instead of a single upload
Test five hooks on the same clip in an afternoon
Launch a paid campaign behind your best organic performer and know what it returned
Show a sponsor planned reach, not just past view counts

proof.label: Kualesa, testing creative before spending
proof.body: Kualesa found its winning angles by testing creative at low spend first, then raised budget and held ROAS at 2.0x. You have a stronger version of that first step already, because your organic numbers tell you which episode landed before a ringgit is spent.

name: Glowith Global
sector: Health and wellness distribution, retail and online
headline: Practical AI wins across a multi-brand portfolio, usable the Monday after.
situation: You bring Korean health brands into Malaysia, led by LactoDay, with an Instagram audience in place and TikTok still being built out. The group also runs a long-standing distribution business with retail pharmacy reach. The job is to make online demand and pharmacy offtake pull in the same direction, from one content effort rather than two.

pathway.name: Owner's Fast-Track
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive built around the owner's calendar, with AI for Marketers (P3) as a follow-on for the content and marketplace side of the team
pathway.why: You need a bit of everything and you need it usable on Monday, not a specialist's version of one topic. Fast-Track gives you enough of each discipline to brief, judge and direct the work.

pillars.title: Retail and online, one message
pillars.body: We build a content system where the same product story drives online sales and asks for the pharmacy purchase too. One shoot, two jobs, and a clear call to action for each.

pillars.title: Two rulebooks, one phrase bank
pillars.body: Probiotic claims answer to the regulator and to platform ad review, and the two do not agree. You leave with a phrase bank that clears both, so a pharmacy label and a TikTok hook can say the same thing.

pillars.title: One portfolio, many brands
pillars.body: A multi-brand house cannot rebuild strategy per product. You leave with a repeatable launch pack that any new brand in the portfolio can be dropped into.

pillars.title: A standard to brief against
pillars.body: As the content and marketplace side of the team grows, output has to be judged in minutes rather than rewritten. We write the briefs, the review checklist and the reporting format with you.

pillars.title: Proof of a real academy

sector: Renovation and fit-out project management, business to business
headline: Turn completed fit-outs into a steady stream of proof that brings the next client.
situation: You supervise and validate commercial fit-outs from Publika, with a large body of completed work behind you. Buying your service is a considered, high-trust decision, and what you are really selling is the removal of risk from someone else's build. Every job you finish is evidence, and the opportunity is to publish that evidence consistently rather than when there happens to be time.

pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive with the founder and whoever supports marketing
pathway.why: You already understand marketing, so the gain is speed and a system rather than theory. Fast-Track covers enough of each discipline for a founder-led firm to run the whole thing without a marketing department.

pillars.title: Projects into proof, on repeat
pillars.body: We build a workflow that turns each completed fit-out into a case story, a set of posts and a sales asset. Site photos and a short voice note become finished content.

pillars.title: Business to business lead generation
pillars.body: Your buyers are developers, brand owners and operators planning a build. We work on reaching them with the specific risk you remove, not with general renovation talk.

pillars.title: Trust before the first call
pillars.body: A high-trust service is won before anyone speaks to you. You leave with content that answers the questions a cautious buyer asks in their head.

pillars.title: A pipeline a founder can run
pillars.body: Enquiries are few and valuable, so each one deserves a proper follow-up sequence. We set up the tracking and the replies so nothing sits unanswered while you are on site.

name: The Earnest Co
sector: Regenerative agriculture, 301 acres across five farm sites
headline: Turn your land, your method and your own story into output you can publish every week.
situation: You already have the thing most food and produce brands pay to invent, a real farm, a real method, and a founder people want to hear from. What is scarce is time, because the same small leadership team runs the land, the buyers and the story. AI is how one person turns 301 acres of provenance into steady output for produce buyers, consumers and the people funding the next phase.

pathway.name: Owner's Fast-Track
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive with you and your farm leads, with two performance modules added
pathway.why: Owner's Fast-Track is built for founders who need practical wins across the whole picture rather than depth in one corner. If you push consumer produce sales, we add Performance Basics and Data and Measurement so that push has real numbers under it.

pillars.title: Provenance is the asset
pillars.body: Your land, your growers and your method are things nobody else can copy or buy. We turn field footage, harvest notes and site visits into a content supply that runs every week.

pillars.title: One founder, weekly output
pillars.body: You should not need a marketing department to publish consistently. You leave with a workflow that turns one hour walking a site into a week of posts, captions and updates.

pillars.title: Two audiences, one system
pillars.body: Consumers want taste, trust and where it came from. Buyers and backers want progress, volume and proof. Same source material, two output formats, built once.

pillars.title: Numbers you can put in a deck
pillars.body: If you take produce direct to consumers, Performance Basics and Data and Measurement give you a plain read on demand and what a lead costs. You will know which stories move buyers, and which ones are worth telling for other reasons.

pathway.why: Your team has real marketing depth, so the flagship's applied spine is the multiplier rather than the introduction. We tune it to multi-brand, multi-market production and to paid short video specifically.

pillars.title: B2B on a consumer feed
pillars.body: Hooks built for a founder scouting an office, delivered in the language of the platform. We build the route from tour footage and member stories through to a real enquiry.

pillars.body: A shared brief and asset structure with brand-specific tone rules, so Common Ground, the Hive and The Cluster stay distinct. The work triples in output without tripling in effort.

pillars.title: Paid short video, built live
pillars.body: Campaign structure, tracking and enquiry handoff set up with your team during the weekend. You leave able to run and read a paid video test in any of your markets.

situation: You have a mature in-house function, an agency roster and an active presence on the platform, so the gap is not knowledge of the channels. It is the operating layer: how fast creative gets produced, tested, read and documented without adding people. Consumer broadband and enterprise sit on different buying cycles, and both run through the same team.

pathway.why: The flagship treats every module as practitioner work rather than orientation, so nothing is spent on ground your team already holds. pillars.title: Creative ops, not creative tips
pillars.body: We build the pipeline: brief to variant set to trafficked ad, with versioning and naming your team keeps. The deliverable is a documented process your team owns.

pillars.title: Testing velocity you can audit

name: Wild Rice Media
headline: Five pathways, one shared library. We map yours with you rather than guessing it.
situation: Every Toggle Bespoke engagement runs off one library of 21 lessons and five pathways through it. Which one fits depends on where you are starting and what you need working by Monday, so we would rather scope it with you than assume it. The five modules below sit in three or more of the five pathways, so wherever you begin, you will do these.

pathway.name: We will map it with you
pathway.shape: One-weekend intensive, scoped in a short conversation first
pathway.why: We do not guess the pathway from a form. A short conversation about your team, your tools and what you need working by Monday decides it, and the depth is set separately on its own dial.

pillars.title: Five ways in
pillars.body: P1 starts with AI literacy and P2 with Marketing Fundamentals. P3 applies AI across a marketing function, P4 is the founder's route through everything at pace, and P5 puts AI inside your operations. Five different starting points, and none of them is a level.

pillars.title: One shared backbone
pillars.body: The five modules below appear in three or more of the five pathways, so the core of the weekend is the same wherever you begin. What changes is what gets built around it.

pillars.title: The depth dial
pillars.body: Every lesson runs on an ELI 15 to 30 setting, so the same module can be a plain introduction or a deep technical build. We set it to the people in the room.

pillars.title: A weekend, not a retainer
pillars.body: The engagement is one intensive weekend where senior marketers build the thing with your team, document it, and support you for 30 days after. You own the accounts, the data and the system afterwards.

modules.name: AI Basics
modules.why: The shared starting point in four of the five pathways, so everyone works from the same picture.

modules.name: Prompting and Tools
modules.why: The practical skill that makes every later module faster, whichever pathway you take.

modules.name: Agentic AI and Claude Code
modules.why: The one module in all five pathways, because handing whole tasks to an agent changes any job.

modules.name: AI CRM and Conversations
modules.why: Every organisation has enquiries and follow-ups, and this is where the quickest wins usually sit.

modules.name: Build Your Workflow
modules.why: The closing module in three pathways, where the weekend becomes a written workflow you keep using.

outcomes: Name which of the five pathways fits you, and say why
List the three tasks in your week AI should take over first
Explain to your team what a one-weekend intensive would actually change
Come to a short scoping call with a specific goal instead of general interest

proof.label: EduKids, e-commerce and education
proof.body: EduKids was stuck under a 4x return on TikTok and hit its 6x target by month two, alongside RM14,000 in monthly website revenue and a steady 5.5% conversion rate. It is relevant to anyone here because the gain came from method, testing and tightening rather than from a bigger budget.
